current.text: He re-signed with the Hawks on a 1-year, 21 million deal.
He is the projected starting guard next to Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu. Each starter is expected to play 30-plus minutes.
Lu Dort is the main threat to his starting spot. If Dort starts, McCollum is the starter most likely to move to the bench.
Experts disagree on the Dort risk. One does not expect Dort to start over him, while another says he could come off the bench.
Atlanta has no true point guard, and he handles the ball more than anyone else on the team. He played point guard after he arrived.
After the trade deadline last season he ranked 63rd. Over the last two months he was top 70 while playing under 30 minutes. For the full season he finished around 93 to 100.
An easy schedule helped Atlanta's strong late-season run last year.

Experts call him undervalued. They say he is worth about 20 to 30 spots above his ADP of about 110 to 118 and target him around picks 80 to 90. He should be better as a locked-in starter on a team pushing for the playoffs.
He goes for about 1 USD in auctions. Josh calls that too low and paid 8 USD for him in a mock auction.
One expert would not draft him at his post-deadline level of 63rd because of his age.
He is a good pick to boost points, threes and assists at a guard spot. There is no worry about him being traded.
Atlanta's fantasy playoff schedule is 4-4-3 games for a March 28 season end. The team has 14 back-to-backs, and resting players is not a concern.
Atlanta is projected for 46 wins and a finish between fourth and eighth in the East.

durable.text: He is a score-first guard, not a pure point guard.
His free throw percentage changes a lot from season to season, and his steals and blocks are low.
Most of his value comes from threes and points. His FG% and rebounds are below the pool.
Quin Snyder runs a high-movement offense that wants many threes and five-out spacing.

note: He costs almost nothing. Yahoo values him at 4 USD with an average cost of 1.0, ESPN at 4 USD with an average cost of 2.1, and he went for 2 USD in our league last season, but experts rank him 20 to 30 spots above his rank of 82 to 106. A bid of up to about 8 USD for a guard who adds threes, points and some assists is reasonable, especially in builds that can absorb his below-average FG%, rebounds and steals. Check early whether he keeps his starting job over Lu Dort and stays near 30 minutes.
